replacement_English: An official letter from %s has arrived.
localization_note: Restore the formality of the official letter. Five original branches share this arrival notice, so the sentence does not assume what the letter proposes.
Use pact for the proposal, as in the Guild correspondence. Preserve proposer first and the opposing faction second. The original Yes/No box asks for a decision.

replacement_English: %s and %s are now allies, with %s as their opponent.
localization_note: Keep the two allies before the named opponent and preserve the completed agreement. Ending with the opponent's role keeps company-name punctuation intact. The counterpart at 382 has no opposing faction.
Offer refused is a clear, neutral result reused in two original branches. The short phrase leaves the identity of the refusing party implicit in the same way as the source.
Fell through reads naturally as the outcome of a pact that failed, distinct from an existing agreement being canceled.
Has been canceled conveys an existing pact being dissolved and preserves the two parties. Keep it distinct from the request to cancel it.
Has asked to cancel keeps the source's request and its emphatic delivery. It does not imply that the pact has already ended.

replacement_English: Will you accept the truce offered by %s?
localization_note: Keep the established Guild term truce. The current question becomes a one-word second row with a long sender name. Ask one natural question that still names the sender and preserves the Yes/No decision.

replacement_English: %s and %s have agreed to a truce.
localization_note: Made peace overstates a ceasefire as a full peace settlement. This common result names both parties, unlike the one-party acceptance at 358.
Replace peace with the Guild's truce terminology. This is the other party's response to the proposal, not a two-party status report.
Flatly carries the force of 突っぱねる and keeps the strong refusal in contrast with the ordinary offer refusal at 352.
Declared war on is the natural construction and preserves who declared and who was targeted. The exclamation point conveys the source's urgency.
Declared war on us accurately addresses a player-side war declaration in the game's existing fleet voice. The preceding letter names the sender without changing which faction is the target.
Joined you can read as ordinary crew recruitment. The source reports a faction coming under the player's authority after a merger offer.
Rejected the merger offer states an explicit decision and stays distinct from the ignored offer at 381. Keep the menu's merger terminology.
Lies suggests something deliberately said to the recipient. The scheme sends misinformation. The notice marks receipt before the separate outcome.

replacement_English: It looks like luring the fleet to %s worked.
localization_note: The name passed to this modal comes from the town catalogue, not the targeted fleet. The original expresses apparent success. Keep the established Lure Fleet vocabulary and name the destination without stating that the fleet has arrived.
Use the established Forge Papers wording and explicit receipt. Keep this distinct from the lure's false report and the later effect on relations.

replacement_English: It looks like the plan turned %s and %s against each other.
localization_note: The current report drops both the scheme's success and the source's apparent-outcome qualifier. Restore both without escalating disagreement to the fighting reported at 370.
They seem to want closer relations keeps the sender's purpose and the source's tentative tone. The letter notice immediately before it supplies the referent.
Someone's schemes seem to be harming our relations keeps the apparent interference, the player's side, and the named party. The sentence is natural in this standalone warning.
Have begun fighting preserves onset and both parties. It leaves a formal declaration to 360 and 361.
The plan seems to have failed preserves the scheme's uncertain result. It works as the failure counterpart to 367 without implying why the plan failed.

replacement_English: In %s, damaging rumors about %s are going around.
localization_note: Rumors of the faction is ambiguous and drops the hostile nature of the rumor. Keep town first and target second in both callers.
Market share has fallen is a natural system result after the town and rumor target have already been named. It leaves the grammatical subject implicit.
The rumor wasn't taken seriously naturally states the failed effect. It makes no claim that the rumor never circulated.

replacement_English: In %s, a broker for %s received the letter.
localization_note: Replace the initial full-width I and simplify acting for to for. Town and faction keep their original order. The letter arrives before the payment and Yes/No decision.
Will you pay? follows the original price explanation. The prompt can stay short and need not duplicate an amount held in a different native call.
Seized conveys the transfer to the player and distinguishes it from the rival's share falling in 378. Market share names what was seized without quantifying the amount.
Name market share and the affected faction while leaving the beneficiary unstated. The result branch is distinct from the explicit takeover at 377.

replacement_English: In %s, it looks like %s bribed your broker!
localization_note: Restore the source's uncertainty and keep town, suspected briber and the player's broker in the same roles. The player is on the receiving end here.
Bribe failed is short, clear status text. It works without adding a reason or treating the rejected payment as a successful attempt.
Ignored the merger offer preserves the lack of a reply, which the source distinguishes from an express rejection. Ordinary line breaks can be refitted.
Formed an alliance conveys the two parties' agreement. This counterpart to 351 has no opposing faction, and the current wording preserves that.
